\ErrataAt{167}{731.02}{368}{$\displaystyle\eta_p(\mathfrak K)W(\chi,\bar p)=\frac{\tau(\chi)}{i^{\operatorname{Tr}(p)}\sqrt{\mathfrak N(\mathfrak m)}}N(|md/a^2|^p)\frac{N(a^p)}{N((md/a)^{\bar p})}$}%

\ErrataAt{79.226}{212.291}{455.774}{Put $\lambda(a)=N(a^p|a|^{-p+iq})$ on $\widehat K^*$, extending $\chi_\infty$.}%
\ErrataAt{79.226}{195.245}{455.774}{For $a\in\widehat{\mathfrak o}^{(\mathfrak m)}$, define $\chi_f(a)=\chi((a))/\lambda(a)$. If $a\equiv b\pmod{\mathfrak m}$, then $a/b\in K^*$}%
\ErrataAt{79.226}{178.199}{455.774}{and $a/b\equiv1\pmod{\mathfrak m}$. The defining property gives $\chi((a/b))=\chi_\infty(a/b)=\lambda(a/b)$.}%
\ErrataAt{79.226}{161.153}{455.774}{Thus the quotient defines a character of $(\widehat{\mathfrak o}/\mathfrak m)^*$ extending the original $\chi_f$.}%

\ErrataAt{79.19}{643.811}{455.81}{In this case the lemma follows by induction. If there are no conditions, partition $V\setminus\{0\}$}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{626.765}{455.81}{by nonzero coordinate sign patterns in a $k$-basis. Otherwise take an inner point $u\in P\cap V_k$.}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{609.719}{455.81}{For $1\le i\le\ell$, partition the nonzero boundary points according to the first vanishing form:}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{592.673}{455.81}{$B_i=\{x\in P\setminus\{0\}: L_i(x)=0,\ L_j(x)>0\text{ for }j<i\}$. The sets $B_i$ are disjoint.}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{575.627}{455.81}{Each $B_i$ is given by rational equalities and strict or weak inequalities in the hyperplane}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{558.581}{455.81}{$L_i=0$, which has dimension less than $n$. The induction hypothesis decomposes $B_i$}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{541.535}{455.81}{into finitely many $k$-rational simplicial cones. Collecting the pieces gives}%

\ErrataAt{79.19}{761.124}{455.81}{\textbf{Proof.} Let $a\in(1+\mathfrak a^{-1}\mathfrak m)^*_{(+)}$. Then $(a-1)\mathfrak a\subseteq\mathfrak m$. At the finite primes dividing}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{744.078}{455.81}{$\mathfrak m$, the ideal $\mathfrak a$ is locally principal with unit ideal image, so $a\equiv1$ there. By positivity, $(a)\in P^{\mathfrak m}$.}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{727.032}{455.81}{Moreover $a\mathfrak a\subseteq\mathfrak a+\mathfrak m=\mathfrak o$. Thus $a\mapsto a\mathfrak a$ defines a mapping}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{709.986}{455.81}{ }%
\TextAt{9}{246.952}{692.94}{\Character{40}1}%
\TextAt{9}{259.995}{692.94}{\Character{43}}%
\TextAt{14}{271.775}{692.94}{a}%
\TextAt{3}{277.758}{697.876}{\Character{0}}%
\TextAt{17}{284.345}{697.876}{1}%
\TextAt{14}{289.077}{692.94}{m}%
\TextAt{9}{298.244}{692.94}{\Character{41}}%
\TextAt{17}{302.796}{691.08}{\Character{40}\Character{43}\Character{41}}%
\NativeArrowAt{319.788}{692.94}{11.955}{19.26}{\longrightarrow}%
\TextAt{14}{342.37}{692.94}{A}%
\TextAt{7}{350.949}{691.147}{int}%
\TextAt{13}{361.792}{692.94}{\Character{58}}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{669.952}{455.81}{It is surjective. If $a\mathfrak a$ is integral in $A$ with $(a)\in P^{\mathfrak m}$ and $a$ totally positive, then $(a-1)\mathfrak a$}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{652.906}{455.81}{is integral and locally lies in $\mathfrak m$ at all primes dividing $\mathfrak m$. Thus $a\in(1+\mathfrak a^{-1}\mathfrak m)^*_{(+)}$.}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{635.86}{455.81}{For two such elements $a,b$, equality $a\mathfrak a=b\mathfrak a$ is equivalent to $a=b\epsilon$ for a unit $\epsilon$.}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{618.814}{455.81}{The quotient $\epsilon=a/b$ is totally positive and satisfies the local ray congruences, so $\epsilon\in E$.}%
\ErrataAt{79.19}{601.768}{455.81}{Conversely multiplication by such a unit does not change the image.}%

\ErrataAt{79.19}{357.912}{455.81}{Here the summations are over the real places of $K$. Let $m_0=\langle\chi,1\rangle$ be the trivial multiplicity.}%

\ErrataAt{79.19}{323.82}{455.81}{The functional equation and the gamma factors give the following orders for $L(L\mid K,\chi,s)$:}%
\ErrataAt{146}{293.476}{355}{$s=0$: order $n^+-m_0$;\qquad $s=-2,-4,\ldots$: order $n^+$,}%
\ErrataAt{141}{256.85}{369}{$s=-1,-3,-5,\ldots$: order $n^-$.}%
